A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RelCon research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, Tables 1–7, and Appendices A.1–A.10. Text and visual inspection support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original RelCon experiments on gait regression, activity classification, and external benchmarks, plus component ablations and appendix loss-function and backbone comparisons.

after.justification: v4 retains the original experimental results in Tables 1–7 and associated figures, including the supplementary experiments in Appendices A.9–A.10.

M1.justification: The learned distance, augmentations, sparsemax, reversible normalization, candidate sampling, and relative contrastive loss procedure remain unchanged. The Equation 6 correction makes the printed expression match the negative-selection rule already described in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use AHMS pretraining and the same six downstream datasets: gait measurements, AHMS activity classification, Opportunity, PAMAP2, HHAR, and MotionSense. Task requirements and sensor-position scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: SimCLR, AugPred, and Accel REBAR in the task-diversity experiments; the Yuan et al. and Haresamudram et al. comparisons in Tables 3–4; and the loss-function and matched-backbone comparisons in Tables 6–7.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 and the appendices retain the same splits, preprocessing, metrics, pretraining budget, encoder configurations, inference windows, probe procedures, and cross-validation designs. No experimental setting is revised.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 5, softer/harder loss comparisons in Table 6, matched-backbone control in Table 7, and classification visualizations and confusion matrices were already present in v1 and remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report five probe retrainings for the task-diversity evaluations, the same seed information, and the same uncertainty reporting and benchmark cross-validation practices. No statistical procedure or disclosure is added.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–7 and plotted findings are unchanged. For example, RelCon's AHMS workout F1 remains 55.28 ± 0.86 in Table 2, and its ResNet-18 PAMAP2 MLP-probe F1 remains 62.5 ± 13 in Table 7.

T1.justification: Equation 6 repairs the incomplete formal negative-set definition: the malformed threshold d(Xanc is completed as d(Xanc, Xpos). This is a local correction consistent with the existing prose; the remaining mathematics and Appendix A.6 complexity analysis are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about a motion foundation model, the learned motif distance and relative contrastive loss, and generalization across classification and regression tasks. No contribution is added or strengthened.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning within-user dynamics, false positive/negative resistance, sensor invariance, and cross-task generalization are retained. The appendix discussions of single-sensor applicability, computational cost, and variable input lengths are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Hardware, training duration, hyperparameters, preprocessing instructions, and implementation references are unchanged. Section 7 still promises code release upon acceptance; v4 does not document a new release or access route.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain unchanged, including the relationship to REBAR, prior accelerometry models, and soft-label contrastive learning. Related-work text moves across a page boundary without substantive revision.

P1.justification: Figure 1's caption is shortened, a second author email is added, and the conference header changes from under review to published. These are limited editorial changes; the section organization and scientific narrative remain stable.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is slightly enlarged using the same underlying image. Caption formatting and early-page reflow change, including keeping the Section 3.2 heading together. All five figures and seven tables are retained without redesigned result displays.

improvement.justification: v4 repairs the incomplete threshold in Equation 6, making the formal definition readable without reconstructing it from the prose. The enlarged Figure 2 and improved heading placement also modestly improve readability. Methods, empirical evidence, interpretations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
